Overall, HUM 112 from Mr. Ilic was neither an effective nor a pleasant experience.

Although that book was the hardest one to read out of the 3 we read, it was the one that I felt really made me "learn" something and intrigued me. It covers topics from the existence of God to the meaning of life, which are topics almost everyone has an opinion on and can ponder about. Like, I am absolutely certain that if I wrote that play myself, and submitted it to a literature board in Bilkent, I would be expelled from school for writing such a horrible and useless book. course: This is a no brainer: the fact that teacher selection matters THIS much, is terrible for this class. But when you put a variety of teachers that range from crazy to perfect, it makes us feel hopeless when we get a bad teacher. They grade horribly no matter how hard you work, they cannot teach the class, etc. And despite all of your efforts, you get a C for example. Meanwhile, you can have a friend who is taking HUM from a very good teacher, who will put in 15% of the work you have, and he/she will get an A or A-. This shouldn't happen. Because of this, HUM has transformed from something that is supposed to intrigue students on literature to a mere gambling game where you throw a dice at the beginning of the semester (teacher selection), which will directly determine your grade for that class, and ultimately your GPA.

I think Dragan Ilic doesn't get the recognition he deserves. He's very knowledgeable about the subjects and can talk for hours. He has a set of rules and is strict about them. Using phones is absolutely forbidden, reading materials are allowed online in class, but they must be printed for quizzes and exams, and he's very strict about being late for class in the first few weeks. But you can easily follow these rules if you're not someone who comes to school just for fun, and I don't think there are too many rules for people of university age. The course flow was enjoyable and engaging. He conducted the midterm as take-home and graded it fairly. Most quizzes and exams asked interpretive questions, and he gave information about the questions he would ask in class. He didn't create a Moodle class and sent everything by email; it would have been more organized if all the content had been collected on Moodle, but you can collect every email he sent in a Drive. My only criticism is that he holds the final exam in the second-to-last week of classes, not during the final exam period, so it clashes with our projects and the architecture jury. Even though we requested flexibility on this, he didn't show any. In short, if you have a normal level of discipline, you will have a very comfortable semester. He has a unique sense of humor; he's a teacher you should experience at least once.
